definition: Generalized regression neural network (GRNN) is a variation to radial basis neural networks.
details: GRNN was suggested by D.F. Specht in 1991. GRNN can be used for regression, prediction, and classification. GRNN can also be a good solution for online dynamical systems. GRNN represents an improved technique in the neural networks based on the nonparametric regression. The idea is that every training sample will represent a mean to a radial basis neuron.

explainer.lead: A generalized regression neural network (GRNN) learns from examples by giving each training sample its own radial basis neuron. It can estimate continuous values, make predictions, or classify inputs, and its design also suits online dynamical systems.

tiers.eli5: Imagine keeping a collection of solved problems and asking that collection for help whenever a new problem arrives. Each saved example contributes an answer through its own small detector, and the network combines those answers. This can help predict a number or choose a category without first describing the relationship with a fixed equation.
tiers.practitioner: Use GRNN for regression, prediction, classification, or online dynamical systems when a nonparametric, example-based model is appropriate. Every training sample becomes the mean of a radial basis neuron, so the training examples remain part of the model rather than being discarded after fitting.
tiers.paperLevel: GRNN is a radial basis neural network variant for nonparametric regression: each training sample x_i represents the mean of a radial basis neuron. D. F. Specht suggested the architecture in 1991. Its applications include regression, prediction, classification, and online dynamical systems.

explainer.example: Suppose three recorded homes have sale prices of 190,000, 210,000, and 230,000. Each record supplies the mean for a radial basis neuron, and their responses are combined for a new home; an illustrative resulting estimate is 210,000.

usedIn.name: Regression
usedIn.detail: Estimating continuous outputs from training examples using nonparametric regression.

usedIn.name: Prediction
usedIn.detail: Producing predictions for new inputs from responses associated with stored samples.

usedIn.name: Classification
usedIn.detail: Assigning inputs to categories with the same example-based network approach.

usedIn.name: Online dynamical systems
usedIn.detail: Modeling systems whose data arrive and evolve over time.

components.name: Training samples
components.detail: The recorded examples that define what the network has learned.

components.name: Radial basis neurons
components.detail: One neuron is associated with each training sample, using that sample as its mean.

components.name: Nonparametric regression
components.detail: The example-based technique underlying the network’s estimates.

components.name: Output
components.detail: The resulting regression estimate, prediction, or classification.

flow: Training samples are retained, and each supplies the mean for a radial basis neuron.
A new input is presented to the network of radial basis neurons.
The neurons’ example-based responses contribute to the network’s nonparametric estimate.
The network produces a regression value, prediction, or classification.
explainer.origin: D. F. Specht suggested GRNN in 1991.
explainer.lineage: GRNN is a variation of radial basis neural networks and an improved neural-network technique based on nonparametric regression.
explainer.whyItMatters: It turns individual training examples directly into radial basis neurons, providing one architecture for regression, prediction, classification, and online dynamical systems.

diagram.caption: Training samples define the radial basis neurons, whose responses support an output for a new input.
